Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

greet verb

also greeting, say hello to, greet someone, return a greeting, hail, exchange greetings

classical

Cic. Planc. 33: cum ille eum salūtāsset, ut fit (Lewis & Short)
Cato Agr. 2.1

salūtō, salūtāre, salūtāvī, salūtātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

greet, say hello to

The everyday word, of saying salvē or avē to someone, in every period. With a second accusative, to hail someone as something: Caesarem salūtāre. The noun salūtātiō is a greeting, and also the morning call on a patron (Cic. Fam. 9.20.3).

Other words

  • cōnsalūtō, cōnsalūtāre, cōnsalūtāvī, cōnsalūtātum — greet warmly; greet one another

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.13: cum inter sē … amīcissimē cōnsalūtāssent (Lewis & Short); Liv. 1.7.1 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 311

  • resalūtō, resalūtāre, resalūtāvī, resalūtātum — return a greeting

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.106 (Lewis & Short); Mart. 5.21.3 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • pater familiās, ubi ad vīllam vēnit, ubi larem familiārem salūtāvit, fundum eōdem diē, sī potest, circumeat

    the master, when he comes to the farm and has greeted the god of the house, should walk round the estate the same day, if he canCato Agr. 2.1

  • salūtārī, adpetī, dēcēdī, adsurgī, dēdūcī, redūcī, cōnsulī

    to be greeted, sought out, made way for, stood up for, escorted there and back, consultedCic. Sen. 63

  • Avum salūtā.

    Say hello to Grandpa.composed

See also hello, say hello to … for me, receive, goodbye.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
